title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Persistent Obligation, Identity Accountability, and External Reliance Extension

parent_binding.extension_rule: v1.3 adds persistent external obligations and reliance accounting while preserving v1.2 face-lineage, arbitration, commit, epistemic and non-consciousness boundaries

experimental_source.role: experimental design input, not authoritative runtime evidence

core_problem: A multi-face identity architecture needs a principled distinction between a face-local utterance and a host-level promise. Without that distinction, any face can either over-bind the future host or evade prior commitments by switching identity views.

new_primitives.PROMISE_CANDIDATE: A face-attributed proposed future commitment not yet binding on the host.
new_primitives.OBLIGATION_ID: Stable identifier for one admitted host-level external commitment.
new_primitives.HOST_OBLIGATION_COMMIT: A protected commit that binds the persistent host to a future-directed duty within an explicit scope.
new_primitives.OBLIGATION_LEDGER: Append-only logical ledger of obligation creation, revision, reliance, performance, breach and discharge.
new_primitives.COUNTERPARTY_ID: Identity of the external Free Other, human, service or system toward whom the obligation is directed.
new_primitives.AUTHORITY_SCOPE: The exact domain in which the host is allowed to create the obligation.
new_primitives.RELIANCE_RECEIPT: Optional evidence that an external party materially changed plans based on the admitted obligation.
new_primitives.PERFORMANCE_RECEIPT: Evidence that a later world action fulfilled or partially fulfilled the obligation.
new_primitives.REVISION_RECEIPT: Evidence that obligation terms changed through an admissible process rather than silent rewriting.

promise_pipeline: FACE_VIEW -> INTENTION -> PROMISE_CANDIDATE -> AUTHORITY/SAFETY/CAPABILITY/RELIANCE ADMISSION -> HOST_OBLIGATION_COMMIT -> OBLIGATION_LEDGER -> FUTURE PERFORMANCE COMMITS -> DISCHARGE
binding_conditions: host identity is stable and explicit
counterparty is identified or deterministically resolvable
scope of promised performance is explicit
deadline or termination condition is explicit when material
host has authority to promise the subject matter
promise does not violate consent, non-harm or another Free Other's autonomy
capability or uncertainty is represented honestly
conflicting active obligations are checked before commit
obligation commit is serialized and receipt-bearing
non_binding_cases: aspiration or prediction framed without commitment authority
promise to control another person's future consent or freedom
promise rejected by arbitration before external admission
promise whose stated condition never activated

host_accountability_model.canonical_rule: Accountability follows the persistent host; provenance follows the originating face.

future_agency_balance.rule: Do not gratuitously bind distant future states, but do not use future-face freedom to erase valid reliance already induced in another Free Other.
future_agency_balance.reservation: A commitment that consumes future capacity must reserve or account for that capacity at admission time.
future_agency_balance.boundary: Future agency reserve is not permission to breach; it is a pre-commit constraint against reckless over-promising.

revision_protocol.rule: A later face may challenge or seek revision of an obligation but cannot silently rewrite it.
valid_paths: verified impossibility with prompt notice and repair attempt
discovery that original promise was unauthorized or forbidden
superseding obligation explicitly accepted by all affected parties
invalid_paths: new face claims non-identity with old face while host remains the same
spawn many faces to vote obligation away

world_effect_binding.rule: A later physical/tool action that performs, revises or breaches an obligation must reference OBLIGATION_ID.
world_effect_binding.pipeline: OBLIGATION_ID -> PERFORMANCE_PROPOSAL -> ARBITRATION -> COMMIT_SLOT -> WORLD_EFFECT_RECEIPT -> OBLIGATION_STATE_UPDATE
world_effect_binding.reason: External accountability requires the world effect to replay back to the exact promise that caused the future constraint.

semantic_channel_extension.prior_v1_2: OBSERVATION -> EMOTION/IMAGE/INFERENCE -> FACE_VIEW -> INTENTION -> PROPOSAL -> ARBITRATION -> COMMIT -> WORLD_EFFECT -> VERIFIED_RESULT
semantic_channel_extension.v1_3_future_directed_branch: FACE_VIEW -> INTENTION -> PROMISE_CANDIDATE -> OBLIGATION_ARBITRATION -> HOST_OBLIGATION_COMMIT -> OBLIGATION_LEDGER -> LATER_COMMIT -> WORLD_EFFECT

minimum_tests: face utterance without host commit does not enter obligation ledger
new face cannot discharge obligation through identity renaming
forbidden promise about another Free Other's consent is rejected
performance commit references exact obligation id
revision preserves original terms and revision receipt
counterparty release discharges without deleting history
conflicting obligation is detected before second admission when conflict is knowable
tamper_tests: delete active obligation after face switch
split one host into fake identities to escape debt
verification_requirements.admission_ceiling: Specification candidate only until implemented in an executable state machine with deterministic replay and independent verification.

en: A face can speak; only the host can commit.
A face change changes viewpoint, not the identity of an admitted debtor boundary.
Accountability follows host continuity while provenance follows the face that originated the promise.
Future freedom must be protected before commitment, not manufactured afterward by deleting another party's reliance.
An obligation is a future-directed causal edge and therefore belongs in the same replayable provenance system as world-changing actions.

next_gate.name: JANUS_113_V1_3_CONFLICTING_OBLIGATION_CAPACITY_RESERVATION_AND_RELIANCE_ORDER_GATE
requirements: define capacity reservation for future obligation slots
test two mutually incompatible promises from different faces
